newsitem.title: new Zealand: CRICKET-NZ ON TOP AT TEA ON 3RD DAY OF TEST VS ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ ON TOP AT TEA ON 3RD DAY OF TEST VS ENGLAND.

text.p: New Zealand were 42 for two at tea on the third day of the third and final cricket test against England at Lancaster Park on Sunday.
The Kiwis, who need to win the test to square the series, established a 118-run first innings lead by bowling England out for 228 soon after lunch.
New Zealand had an early setback when opener Blair Pocock played a ball from Dominic Cork on to his stumps in the first over of the innings.
Then Adam Parore, who had spent 84 minutes and 55 balls over eight, was caught behind off Darren Gough in the final over before tea.
Opener Bryan Young was on 29 at tea.
England captain Mike Atherton had earlier become the seventh English player to bat through a completed test innings when he made 94 not out.

At lunch he was on 92, but Andrew Caddick was caught at gully in the second over after the resumption and last man Phil Tufnell managed to deprive his captain of the strike, and eventually edged a catch to second slip, leaving Atherton high and dry.
It is the 34th time a batsman has remained unbeaten through a complete test innings.
Left armer Geoff Allott recorded his best figures, four for 74, with medium pacer Nathan Astle taking two for 26 and the other four bowlers all picking up one wicket apiece.
